title: Meeting Rooms
statement_md:
You're given a list of meetings where `intervals[i] = [start, end]` means meeting `i` runs from time `start` up to, but not including, time `end`.

Return `true` if one person could attend every meeting — that is, if no two meetings overlap. A meeting that ends at time `t` does **not** conflict with one that starts at time `t`.

examples.explanation: The first meeting ends exactly when the second begins, which is allowed.
Both meetings are in progress at time 4.
Sorted by start time the meetings are [1,3], [3,7], [7,9] — back to back with no overlap.

tests.explain_on_fail: Back-to-back meetings that only touch at an endpoint.
Unsorted input that has no overlap once sorted.
One meeting sits entirely inside another.
The overlap only shows up after sorting by start time.
A large input with no overlaps — sort once, then compare neighbours.
A large input in which exactly one pair of meetings overlaps.

editorial_md:
### Intuition
After sorting meetings by start time, any overlap must involve two *neighbouring* meetings: if meeting `i` doesn't overlap meeting `i + 1`, it can't overlap anything that starts even later.

### Algorithm
Sort by start. For each consecutive pair, a conflict exists when the later meeting starts before the earlier one ends (`start < previous end`). Touching endpoints are fine because intervals are half-open.

```python
def canAttendMeetings(intervals):
    intervals = sorted(intervals)
    for i in range(1, len(intervals)):
        if intervals[i][0] < intervals[i - 1][1]:
            return False
    return True
```

### Complexity
O(n log n) time for the sort, O(n) space for the sorted copy.

hints.body_md: If the meetings were listed in order of start time, which pairs would you need to compare?
Sort by start time. Then only adjacent meetings can conflict: check whether each meeting starts before the previous one ends.

```
sort intervals by start
for i in 1..n-1:
    if intervals[i].start < intervals[i-1].end: return false
return true
```
Strictly less-than, because touching is allowed: `if intervals[i][0] < intervals[i - 1][1]: return False`.
